title: harmonize-v1-chat-completions-params-stream-safety-shim
author: Diego Morales
release_notes: Backfills OpenAI /v1/chat.completions parity for params, roles, stop arrays, and logprob fallback; improves stream backpressure handling and toolcall handshake resiliency; no user-facing breaking changes expected.
description:
Motivation: customers building on the OpenAI /v1/chat.completions surface reported subtle incompatibilities around parameter aliases (role hints, presence/temperature mappings), inconsistent stop-array handling in streaming mode, and missing logprob fallbacks when models were served by variant kernels. This PR implements a lightweight compatibility shim that (1) translates incoming v1 parameters into Redwood's internal serving config deterministically, (2) normalizes role aliases and enforces role ordering preservation, (3) coalesces stop token arrays and applies a deterministic stop prioritization for stream fragments, (4) provides a graceful logprob fallback path for quantized/approx kernels, and (5) hardens the stream coordinator's backpressure and resume handshake for tool/function call fragments to reduce dropped fncall payloads.

What this changes (high level): translated-params: a small param-mapping layer that accepts OpenAI-style fields (temperature, top_p, presence_penalty aliases, role hints) and emits a canonical Redwood inference config; role normalization: map common role aliases (assistant/bot/system => standardized role tags) while preserving user-provided metadata fields; stop handling: merge duplicate/overlapping stop arrays and attach a compact stop index to fragments so the stream reconciler deterministically decides cutpoints; logprob path: when the fast kernel cannot produce token-level logprobs we synthesize a lightweight fallback by using the approximate scorer and mark the token with a provenance field so downstream tooling can opt out; stream coordinator: introduce a small datagram ACK and a resume token for fncall fragments so tool outputs spanning multiple stream chunks are reassembled without duplication on transient reconnects; structured output shaping: add a permissive JSON-sanitizer that attempts to coerce obvious single-object responses into valid JSON while preserving raw-text fallthrough.

Commits (summary): - 7b3f2a1 add param-mapping layer and unit tests for alias permutations - f9c4d27 implement stop-array coalescer and deterministic stop indexer - a11e0d3 add logprob fallback shim and provenance tagging - c3d9ee5 stream coordinator: backpressure ACK/resume token and integration tests - d7b44bf structured-output sanitizer and docs examples - e2f6a5c update python/ts SDK proxied examples and compatibility note

Files changed (high level): src/compat/v1_chat_shim.py (new): param translation, role normalization, stop coalescer; runtime/stream/coordinator.go (mod): ACK/resume token, backpressure tuning; runtime/inference/logprob_fallback.go (new): approximate scorer fallback path; sdk/python/openai_proxy.py (mod): proxy entrypoint and examples; docs/openai_compat.md (mod): compatibility guide and migration notes; tests/integration/test_v1_chat_compat.py (new): end-to-end scenarios including toolcall fragmentation; webui/playground/compat_demo.json (new): example prompts for QA.

Testing and CI: local unit and integration test suite expanded. CI status: build: pass, unit: pass, integration: flaky@first-run (tests/integration/test_v1_chat_compat.py retried once and passed), lint: pass, e2e-demo-deploy: pass. We exercised the shim against a small matrix of model variants (fp16, int8-approx, kv-cache-optimized) and confirmed behavior parity for the canonical prompts in docs/openai_compat.md.

Review thread (high level): Priya Kapoor requested clearer guarantees around stop priority and asked for an explicit note about non-deterministic stop resolution when model tokenization boundaries overlap. Author reply: added deterministic stop indexer and documented the caveat in docs/openai_compat.md. Priya approved after documentation update. Ethan Brooks raised perf concerns about added branching in hot path (param mapping per-request). Author reply: moved the hot mapping into a lightweight fast-path (frozen mapping table) and added microbenchmarks showing <1% p99 latency delta at 128 concurrency. Ethan requested a benchmark artifact; artifact uploaded and linked. Ethan approved. Sofia Martinez asked for more robust resume semantics for tool fragments (edge cases with reconnects and partial writes). Author reply: added resume token, ACK semantics, and an integration test that simulates reconnects; Sofia approved with one minor nit fix (renamed resume_token -> stream_resume_token) which is included.

Risk and rollout plan: This PR is behind a feature flag (compat.v1_chat_shim) enabled for internal staging and opt-in for early access customers. Gradual rollout: stage -> canary -> 10% prod -> 100% over 7 days with close monitoring (latency, error-rate, mismatch-rate against golden responses). We added metrics for: compat.param_map_rate, compat.stop_coalesce_count, compat.logprob_fallback_rate, stream.resume_retries. No breaking changes expected; default behavior remains unchanged unless the feature flag is enabled.

Notes and follow-ups: Add an opt-out header for customers who prefer strict legacy behavior; follow-up ticket ENG-8523 created to add RBAC guard for the shim in Private deployments. Also plan a small docs addendum showing how to interpret provenance-tagged logprobs in the Console.

Merge: squashed and merged to main after approvals and green CI. Merge commit references the Linear tasks ENG-8421 and ENG-8437.
